theme: Graphite GPU backend and Skia m152
highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.152.0 introduces the Graphite GPU backend, updates the engine to Skia m152, and closes several memory-safety and performance gaps.
highlights_body: Graphite bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn land alongside async pixel-readback on both Ganesh and Graphite surfaces. Memory leaks in SKRegion, SKPixmap and SKImage are fixed, and hot paths in SKData and GetEncodedText shed unnecessary copies. Nano Server gains FreeType font support, and the MSVC environment initialization overhead on Windows is eliminated.

bullets.detail: The bundled engine advances to Chrome milestone 152, with upstream m151 stability merges also folded in.

bullets.lead: Binding generation is now cross-platform deterministic
bullets.detail: The generated P/Invoke binding files now produce identical output regardless of the OS running the generator, eliminating spurious diffs on non-Windows machines.

bullets.lead: Graphite GPU backend: Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn
bullets.detail: New bindings expose the Graphite rendering pipeline for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn backends, unlocking the next-generation GPU renderer alongside the existing Ganesh backend.

bullets.lead: Async pixel readback on SKImage and SKSurface
bullets.detail: A new backend-neutral RequestReadPixels API allows async, non-blocking pixel readback from both Ganesh and Graphite surfaces.
A dedicated NuGet package wires up the Silk.NET Vulkan interop layer so Vulkan-backed SkiaSharp surfaces can be created without writing manual P/Invoke.
The underlying SKRegion was not rooted during iteration and could be collected mid-loop, leading to heap corruption. The region is now held alive for the iterator's lifetime.

bullets.lead: Native use-after-free in SKPixmap.ExtractSubset and With*
bullets.detail: The pixel-source owner was not rooted across ExtractSubset and the With* mutation methods, allowing the GC to collect the backing buffer while the pixmap was still alive.

bullets.lead: CoTaskMem pixel-buffer leak in SKImage.Create failure path
bullets.detail: When raster image creation failed, the CoTaskMem buffer allocated for the pixel data was not freed. The failure path now releases the buffer correctly.

SKData.SaveTo avoids a double buffer copy by writing directly to the destination. GetEncodedText eliminates an intermediate string allocation in the null-terminated fast path. SKRuntimeEffectUniforms pre-sizes its uniform lookup map to the known count, avoiding rehashing.
The reflection-based check that decides whether to skip handle dictionary registration is now cached per type rather than repeated on every allocation, reducing overhead in object-heavy workloads.
All .sln solution files are converted to the new .slnx format supported by modern .NET SDK and Visual Studio tooling.

bullets.lead: FreeType font support on Nano Server
bullets.detail: Nano Server containers now get working text rendering via FreeType, fixing a long-standing gap where fonts were unavailable in that environment.

bullets.lead: Windows MSVC environment initialized once per build
bullets.detail: The MSVC toolchain environment is now set up once per native build job instead of once per compilation unit, cutting Windows native build times.

bullets.lead: New containerized CI test legs: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, Nano Server
bullets.detail: Adds dedicated CI legs for Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Nano Server containers so regressions on these targets are caught before release.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: Added FreeType font support for Nano Server containers, closing a long-standing text rendering gap
contributor_summaries.mmitche: Eliminated the repeated MSVC environment initialization to speed up Windows native builds
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Implemented the Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn
